_about: Critical frames on cultural institutions, one per museum type or funding situation. Each frame carries word-for-word quotations with author, title, publication, date and address, written by tools/build_critique_frames.py from quotes checked against the source page. Three of them (Groys, Žižek, Varoufakis) are single-author frames written into that script. tools/attach_critiques.py puts them on the records they apply to as critiques of kind theory.

frames.target: National, city and war museums, and museums of history
frames.impact: Ask whose past the permanent display tells, who paid for the telling, and what the galleries leave out.

quotes.text: The museum must render the tank useless upon entry, the way old cannons are filled with cement before being displayed in parks.
quotes.author: Hito Steyerl
quotes.title: A Tank on a Pedestal: Museums in an Age of Planetary Civil War
quotes.context: On a Soviet war memorial tank driven off its pedestal into the war in Donbas.

quotes.text: The new right-wing government realized that museums, as privileged spaces of national self-representation, had to be more closely controlled, since they were perceived as too cosmopolitan and independent.
quotes.author: Edit András
quotes.title: Vigorous Flagging in the Heart of Europe: The Hungarian Homeland under the Right-Wing Regime
quotes.context: On the national museums of Hungary under its right-wing government.

quotes.text: Although used as a museum, the Humboldtforum, it is first and foremost a symbolic building that aims to contribute to identity and express a new national self-image.
quotes.author: Philipp Oswalt
quotes.title: Building a National House
quotes.context: On the Humboldt Forum in Berlin.

frames.impact: Ask how the collection was acquired, whose land the specimens came from, and who pays for the displays.

quotes.text: To this day, natural history dioramas tend to compose three-dimensional tableaus of wild nature, while anthropogenic visions of urbanisation, deforestation, mining, extinction, or pollution remain an absolute exception.
quotes.author: Anna-Sophie Springer, Etienne Turpin
quotes.title: Necroaesthetics: Denaturalising the Collection

quotes.text: In the context of natural history collections, ecologising the museum means accounting for and negotiating with the various violent modes through which "collecting" took place.
quotes.author: Anna-Sophie Springer, Etienne Turpin
quotes.title: Necroaesthetics: Denaturalising the Collection

quotes.text: References to "Nature's treasure house" present the museum as an inventory of nature, as a domain separate from humans (Thackray & Press 2013).
quotes.author: Fiona R. Cameron
quotes.title: Theorising More-Than Human Collectives for Climate Change Action in Museums
quotes.context: On the Natural History Museum, London.

frames.impact: Ask how the objects arrived, who claims them, and what the museum says about that in its own galleries and accounts.

quotes.text: The Musée de l’Homme, especially in its golden age, was a mechanism connecting that picturesque, aerial view of the modern city with a panoptic view of Others and their objects.
quotes.author: Natasha Marie Llorens
quotes.title: The Colonial Museum

quotes.text: The earlier assumption of epistemological authority does not extend comfortably within the post-colonial situation.
quotes.author: Clémentine Deliss
quotes.title: Collecting Life's Unknowns

quotes.text: The importance of preserving a huge collection of cultural heritage from colonial history did not appear to be a factor in the debate.
quotes.author: Mirjam Kooiman
quotes.title: The Dutch VOC Mentality. Cultural Policy as a Business Model
quotes.context: On the Dutch state’s cuts to the Tropenmuseum and its colonial collection.

frames.target: Museums and centres of modern and contemporary art
frames.impact: Read the board and the donor list against the programme: whose dissent has room here, and whose does not.

quotes.text: But whenever freedom is privatized it is also precarious: it shifts the right to dissent to a dependence on well-intentioned patrons.
quotes.author: Philippe Pirotte and Els Silvrants-Barclay
quotes.title: The Fifth Estate: On Museums, Public Imagination and the Vanishing Space for Collectivity

quotes.text: The Global Guggenheim is a cultural refinery for a set of post-democratic oligarchies, as are the countless international biennials tasked with upgrading and reeducating the surplus population.
quotes.author: Hito Steyerl
quotes.title: Politics of Art: Contemporary Art and the Transition to Post-Democracy

quotes.text: In the case of the 2019 Whitney Biennial, Warren B. Kanders was a peripheral figure easily sacrificed to preserve the broader unity of the philanthropic apparatus.
quotes.author: Mostafa Heddaya and Rijin Sahakian
quotes.title: Recolonize This Place

frames.target: Biennials, triennials and large periodic exhibitions
frames.impact: Read who pays for each national or sponsored presentation, and what the host city is left with.

quotes.text: The organization of the Venice Biennale’s pavilions should be interpreted as a 118-year-old cultural allegory of the rise of the nation-state.
quotes.author: Jonas Staal
quotes.title: Art. Democratism. Propaganda.

quotes.text: A pavilion at Venice is, of course, a propaganda vessel, a tool for soft power.

quotes.title: 15th Venice Architecture Biennale, “Reporting from the Front”

frames.target: Museums whose funders carry a flag
frames.impact: Where a flag names an industry, ask what the gift buys the giver, and who sits on the board that accepts it.

quotes.text: “Philanthropy” thus becomes part reputation management, part real estate strategy, but rarely community care.
quotes.author: Philippe Pirotte and Els Silvrants-Barclay
quotes.title: The Fifth Estate: On Museums, Public Imagination, and the Vanishing Space for Collectivity (A Report from Flanders, Belgium), Part 2

quotes.text: Right now, too many large cultural institutions around the world allow oil sponsors to brand their entranceways, their catalogues and their events.
quotes.author: Mel Evans and Kevin Smith (Liberate Tate)
quotes.title: Imagining a Culture Beyond Oil at the Paris Climate Talks

quotes.text: Who should sit on the boards? And I say: Don’t make trustees out of carbon and oil kings. Or out of the punishment monarchy.
quotes.author: Macarena Gómez-Barris
quotes.title: Un-Earthing Extractive Architectures

frames.target: Museums of modern and contemporary art, biennials and festivals
frames.impact: Read a museum’s event calendar and curatorial turnover against what it actually keeps, conserves and pays for.

quotes.author: Boris Groys
quotes.title: Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk
quotes.text: Thus, our art museums became huge garbage cans of history in which things were kept and exhibited that had no use anymore in real life: sacral images of past religions or status objects of past lifestyles.

quotes.author: Boris Groys
quotes.title: Entering the Flow: Museum between Archive and Gesamtkunstwerk
quotes.text: A new curator is a new dictator who erases the traces of the previous dictatorship. In this way, contemporary museums continually morph from spaces for permanent collections into stages for temporary curatorial projects—temporary Gesamtkunstwerks.

frames.strategy: The gift that follows the taking
frames.target: Institutions funded by donors whose money carries a flag
frames.impact: Where a flag names an industry, ask what the gift was repairing, and for whom.

quotes.author: Slavoj Žižek
quotes.title: Nobody has to be vile
quotes.text: Remember Andrew Carnegie, who employed a private army to suppress organised labour in his steelworks and then distributed large parts of his wealth for educational, cultural and humanitarian causes, proving that, although a man of steel, he had a heart of gold? In the same way, today’s liberal communists give away with one hand what they grabbed with the other.

quotes.author: Slavoj Žižek
quotes.title: Nobody has to be vile
quotes.text: According to liberal communist ethics, the ruthless pursuit of profit is counteracted by charity: charity is part of the game, a humanitarian mask hiding the underlying economic exploitation.

frames.target: Biennials, festivals and touring exhibitions, and the cities that host them
frames.impact: Read a festival’s balance with its host city, and its critique against its sponsor list.

quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.title: Artists should be ‘feared by the powerful’, says former Greek finance minister
quotes.context: Closing the sixth Moscow Biennale, he began by asking the hall to look at the money in their pockets:
quotes.text: Take a euro note out and have a look at it. […] Just look at it aesthetically. What do you see? A very boring design.

quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.title: Artists should be ‘feared by the powerful’, says former Greek finance minister
quotes.context: The bridges and arches on the notes are ‘figments of some second-rate artist’s imagination’, he said, because the EU’s members could not agree on whose cultural treasures should appear on them. Worse than art created by committee, though, are the attempts of bureaucrats and big businesses to appropriate it:
quotes.text: Art must not be anodyne, culture cannot be decorative. [Artists] should be feared by the powerful in our society; if you are not, you are not doing your job properly.

quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.title: Artists should be ‘feared by the powerful’, says former Greek finance minister
quotes.context: In an aside, he also knocked
quotes.text: forums in which the stars are the postmodernist curators inviting economists to give a lecture to artists.

quotes.author: Yanis Varoufakis
quotes.title: “We Come Bearing Gifts”—iLiana Fokianaki and Yanis Varoufakis on Documenta 14 Athens
quotes.context: In conversation with iLiana Fokianaki on Documenta 14 in Athens.
quotes.text: Documenta took a great deal more from Athens—from both its private and public sector—than it gave. […] When Documenta comes here and talks about neoliberalism with no mention of Deutsche Bank, Société Générale, the awful Troika process, the Eurogroup, etc., it is choosing to be irrelevant.
